findings.concrete-fix: In src/review.ts, refuse a declared environment name that is one of CREDENTIAL_STORE_REDIRECTIONS' five names before anything is created, next to the refuseExtraAllowlist call: `const pointer = harnessEnvironment.find((e) => CREDENTIAL_STORE_REDIRECTIONS.some((r) => r.name === e.name)); if (pointer !== undefined) return { ok: false, reason: ... }` (CREDENTIAL_STORE_REDIRECTIONS is already exported from src/exec/env.ts). Re-applying the redirect override after the injection loop also closes it and restores buildChildEnv's ordering invariant; routing the injection through buildChildEnv's own extraAllowlist would close it too but would undo the deliberate choice to keep these variables away from `npm ci`. Either way add a third dangerousState to witness/m6-p7-harness-environment-declared.json mutating that refusal, and extend the named test to assert the reviewer's HOME is still under scrub-env when the executor declares HOME.
evidence: src/review.ts:541-550 injects the executor's declared environment into childEnv.env AFTER buildChildEnv has returned. src/exec/env.ts:buildChildEnv sets env[redirection.name] = target LAST and unconditionally, and its own comment states why: 'The override runs last and unconditionally, so a pointer that is also (wrongly) allowlisted still ends up redirected.' The new injection runs after that, so it defeats the ordering.

The only guard on a declared name is refuseExtraAllowlist(harnessEnvironment, 'reason-required'), which walks REFUSED_CHILD_ENV_VOCABULARIES (gh-token, dangerous, egress). grep of src/gates/credentials.ts: none of HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, GH_CONFIG_DIR, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM appears in any of the three vocabularies (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT is there; GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL is not).

MEASURED, arm 1 (HOME, a directory pointer). Dispatch through test/fixtures/review-dispatch/stub-codex-executor.mjs with TIPHYS_STUB_DECLARE=HOME, the kernel's HOME set to a scratch dir holding .git-credentials with the string SECRET-TOKEN. Output: 'exit 1' (only the expected no-served-model problem), 'refused? false', 'reviewer HOME: /tmp/probe-kernel-home-zSobYH', 'kernel real HOME: /tmp/probe-kernel-home-zSobYH', 'HOME IS THE KERNEL REAL HOME: true', 'reviewer could read HOME/.git-credentials: "https://x:SECRET-TOKEN@github.com"'. The same probe with no extra declaration prints 'HOME IS THE KERNEL REAL HOME: false' and 'reviewer could read HOME/.git-credentials: null', so the baseline is correct and the declaration is what breaks it.

MEASURED, arms 2 and 3 (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, a file pointer, and XDG_CONFIG_HOME, a directory pointer), so the class reddens under structurally different members. dispatchReview called directly with an executor declaring both with a reason and a child that dumps its own process.env: 'dispatch ok: true' (no refusal, no recorded problem), 'GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL the reviewer got: /tmp/probe-val-uOoDTM/real-gitconfig', 'XDG_CONFIG_HOME the reviewer got: /tmp/probe-val-uOoDTM/real-xdg', 'GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL IS THE KERNEL REAL ONE: true', 'XDG_CONFIG_HOME IS THE KERNEL REAL ONE: true'. HOME and GH_CONFIG_DIR stayed under scrub-env in that run, confirming only the declared names are overwritten.

src/review.ts:340-345 reviewChildEnv calls buildChildEnv with NO extraAllowlist, so the declared environment never passes through the module that owns the pointer discipline: it is written onto the returned map instead. src/exec/env.ts:permittedChildEnvNames, which enumerates every name the constructed environment may hold, therefore does not describe the environment the reviewer actually receives.

plugin/src/review.ts declares no `environment` at all (grep: no hit), so the only shipped executor that uses this field is adapters/codex/review.ts with CODEX_API_KEY, which is why the severity is medium.

src/exec/env.ts module comment states the consequence this re-opens, and calls it forbidden: 'Dropping any of them is FORBIDDEN ... A dropped HOME does not remove the home directory; the child's tools fall back to the real one ... so gh resolves $HOME/.config/gh/hosts.yml, git resolves ~/.gitconfig, ~/.netrc and ~/.git-credentials, and every default credential path RETURNS. An environment-only scrub that drops pointers leaves the credential stores in place, which is exactly finding M2R-004.' Overwriting a pointer with the real value is strictly worse than dropping it.

The refusal that does exist was shown to be the only one: mutating `if (refusedEnvironment !== undefined)` to `if (false && refusedEnvironment !== undefined)` reddens the named test on the GH_TOKEN arm ('The input did not match the regular expression /declares an environment the kernel refuses: the allowlist extension entry GH_TOKEN/'), and restoring it returns the suite to green. So the GH_TOKEN half is guarded and the pointer half is not guarded at all.
findings.analysis: MEDIUM rather than high because the path is narrower than the shipped artefacts: adapters/codex/review.ts declares only CODEX_API_KEY, so nothing this phase ships reaches the hole. It needs a project-supplied executor module (the extension point this phase newly opens, selected by charter.yaml review-executor or --executor) to declare a pointer name. It is not an adversarial path though: ReviewExecutor.environment is documented as 'the variables the harness needs beyond the kernel's scrubbed allowlist to authenticate', and HOME is the name an adapter author is most likely to declare in good faith, since most CLIs read their config and credentials from $HOME. The kernel, not the adapter, is the thing that is supposed to refuse a dangerous widening, and here it accepts one with a green suite.

delivery/work-history/m6-p7.md:168-170 records the property that makes this matter: 'unknown keys are silently accepted, exit 0, so a key is only proved by a type error'. A future typo in a key name would therefore widen the sandbox silently; the argv test would redden only until the same typo was pasted into its expected literal, after which it passes while the sandbox it guards is wider.

Not raised higher: the keys AS DELIVERED were verified by measurement against the installed CLI and the per-key error text is quoted at delivery/work-history/m6-p7.md:170-177, and the offline bounds check at :178-184 measured the resulting sandbox (writes to a sibling directory, /tmp and $TMPDIR refused 'Read-only file system'; curl and node https failed DNS; controls with workspace-write defaults wrote all four places and with network_access=true reached the network). So this is durability of the guard, not a wrong artefact today.

findings.concrete-fix: In configuredReviewExecutor, resolve charter.yaml against the repository root rather than the passed directory (the dispatch already runs `git rev-parse --show-prefix` for exactly this reason), or state in the refusal that only the current directory was looked in.
evidence: src/review.ts:configuredReviewExecutor joins 'charter.yaml' onto the directory it is given, and src/commands/review.ts sets `const project = process.cwd()`.
dispatchReview itself supports a cwd below the repository root: it runs `git rev-parse --show-prefix` and applies the prefix to locate the review directory inside the worktree.

MEASURED: a scratch repo with review-executor in charter.yaml at its root, dispatch run from a subdirectory: 'exit 1', 'tiphys review: no --executor was given and /tmp/probe-cfg-rhMva3/project/sub/charter.yaml could not be read: ENOENT'. It fails closed, which is why this is low: no silent fallback, exit 1, and --executor is a workaround.

deviations-judged.reasoning: The limit is in the harness, not the code, and it is declared at every place a later reader would look rather than papered over: adapters/codex/review.ts:159-175 states the measured property and that the requested model is never a fallback; delivery/work-history/m6-p7.md:211-222 says 'p7-observe's first half ... is NOT MET with Codex 0.159.2'; the 'Not done' section repeats it and names what would unblock it; and the live record at :297-303 carries "model": null and "family": "unknown". Verified, not taken on the work history's word: test/codex-review.test.ts:145 asserts the measured property (no row of the real capture carries a `model` key at any depth) and passes, and mutating the observer to read a model out of an agent_message row reddens the named test ('actual: gpt-6-luna, expected: null').
